WRS Raipur · Spring & Wagon QC · the administrator, on the laptop

Administrator walk — every screen, step by step

Before you start — five minutes, once

  1. On the shop PC, double‑click START.cmd; it prints the address for the tablet.
  2. On the tablet, turn mobile data off and join the shop Wi‑Fi.
  3. Install the certificate on the tablet once — server\certs\lan‑cert.crt, as in TABLET_TRUST.md — so the address opens with no warning and the camera and offline mode are allowed.
  4. Open the address START.cmd printed and accept Add to home screen.
  5. Sign in with the administrator account.

Then go step by step. Each step shows the screen as it should look, the taps in order, what must be on your screen, and what to suspect when it is not. Tick Seen it only when you saw it.

People

5.1 – 5.3

Sign in as the administrator. Accounts, the roster, what each role holds.

5.1

User accounts

Seen it

Do

  1. Sign in with the account you were given.
  2. Tap User Accounts.
  3. Deactivate an account, try to sign in as it elsewhere, reactivate it.

You must see

  • The accounts with their roles; each can be deactivated and reactivated.
  • A deactivated account cannot sign in; reactivated, it can.
  • Creating an account asks for a one-time code first.

What it proves

People change; the record does not. An account is switched off, never deleted, so everything it wrote stays attributed.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:16 pm

  • the accounts are listed
  • each can be deactivated and reactivated

By hand: Creating an account with the form (one-time code) is done by hand.

5.2

Roster import — three ways

Seen it

Do

  1. Open Roster import.
  2. Paste three lines — name, ID, role — or pick the office's CSV with the file button. Tap Preview.

You must see

  • A file picker for the office's CSV; a paste box; the form at the top for one at a time.
  • The preview lists the three with their roles; problems, if any, are named line by line.
  • Confirm (one-time code) → three printable slips with first-time passwords.

What it proves

The shop's roster comes from a spreadsheet; it should not be retyped.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:23 pm

  • a file picker for the office's CSV
  • the preview lists the three

By hand: Confirming the import is done by hand so the demonstration accounts stay as they are.

5.3

What each role holds

Seen it

Do

  1. Scroll to What each role holds.

You must see

  • The capability table, read-only, with the note saying why: who may do what is fixed in the system. The administrator cannot release a wagon.
  • To change a person's access, change their role on their row.

What it proves

Roles are policy, not settings — nobody can grant themselves the exit gate.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:29 pm

  • the table is on the page
  • read-only by design, with the note saying why
  • shows the admin cannot release a wagon

Rules and instruments

5.4 – 5.6

The checklist, the gauges, the PC's readiness.

5.4

Checklist rules

Seen it

Do

  1. Checklist Rules. Read the blue box. Pick a wagon type.
  2. Add a shop line with a reason and a source; withdraw it.

You must see

  • The blue box: What it is · What you can do · When.
  • The items per wagon type with their standard and expected quantity; a shop line can be added with a reason and where the figure comes from; each change recorded under your name.

What it proves

The exit gate enforces what this screen holds. The standard's items cannot be removed; the shop's own lines can be added and withdrawn — on the record.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:31 pm

  • the blue box: what it is, what you can do, when
  • a shop line can be added with a reason and source
5.5

The gauge register

Seen it

Do

  1. User Accounts → scroll to the bottom: Gauge register.

You must see

  • Four gauges: ISG‑01, OSG‑01, OSG‑02 in calibration; SSG‑02 with its certificate number 1251122‑04‑125 and NOT RECORDED.
  • The amber banner: how many readings were judged with an instrument whose calibration is not established.
  • The drift box, one line per finding: OSG‑02 & OSG‑01 · the two gauges on this kind disagree by 1.5 mm … put both against the master — once for HS outer, once for NLB outer.
  • Record calibration on SSG‑02 with the certificate's dates → the amber note on the bench goes.

What it proves

The instruments and their papers, transcribed from the real labels on the bench; a gauge drifting shows up from the record, not from a calibration visit.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:36 pm

  • four gauges
  • SSG-02 shows its certificate number
  • and NOT RECORDED for its calibration
  • the drift box, one line per finding: "2 findings: a gauge reads a millimetre or more from the shop's other gauges on the same kind of spring. Put them against…"
  • one line per finding (2) — the same pair once per spring kind, not once per gauge

By hand: Recording SSG‑02's calibration is left undone in this check so the bench keeps showing the amber note.

5.6

Deployment readiness, first

Seen it

Do

  1. DRM Dashboard as the administrator. Tap Check now.

You must see

  • Deployment readiness and Storage are the first two panels, before Shop Floor — Right Now.
  • Every row a plain sentence: backup, cloud copy, manual (each document named), demo passwords (red on the demonstration record, saying why they still sign in — SEED_DEMO_USERS), restarts, audit chain, storage.

What it proves

The administrator sees whether the PC is fit before anyone else sees a figure.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:41 pm

  • Deployment readiness is on the dashboard
  • and it comes before Shop Floor — Right Now
  • rows for backup, manual, demo passwords, audit chain
  • the demo-passwords row says why they still sign in

If it is not there

  • Demo passwords green on the demo record: the .env line was removed — that is what production wants, but the demo accounts then cannot sign in.

Your own account

5.7 – 5.8

Password and authenticator — the same for every role.

5.7

Changing your password

Seen it

Do

  1. Top right: Password (the key icon, labelled).

You must see

  • The panel opens in full over the page — old password, new password, confirm — not cut off under the header.
  • After a change the old password stops working; the new one works. The same for every role.

What it proves

Every person can keep their own password without an administrator.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:52 pm

  • the panel is fully on screen, not under the header
  • old and new password boxes

By hand: The change itself is by hand; the demo password is left as it is.

5.8

The authenticator

Seen it

Do

  1. Top right: Authenticator (the shield icon, labelled) → Start setup.

You must see

  • Authenticator setup: a QR to scan with an authenticator app and a box for the six-digit code.
  • A wrong code is refused; the right one enrols; sign-in then needs the code — and one-time codes for releases and overrides come from the app instead of the screen.

What it proves

For the shop the code can come from the person's own phone, with no network at all.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:54 pm

  • the enrolment panel opens in full
  • a QR to scan with the app, and a box for the code

By hand: Enrolling needs an authenticator app on a phone; left undone in this check.

Stores, passports, history

5.9 – 5.11

What the administrator keeps for the shop.

5.9

Stores — add a part, restock

Seen it

Do

  1. Stores & Depot Inventory → + Add a part → code, name, category, bin → save.
  2. Restock it by 10; try 1.5.

You must see

  • The part appears in the list.
  • Restock 10 → the stock rises by 10; restock 1.5 → refused (whole units only).

What it proves

Stores can be kept up to date by the stores clerk without a programmer.
